articles.title: Apple’s chip chief might be the next exec to leave
articles.summary: Apple’s chip chief, Johny Srouji is “seriously considering” leaving for another company in the near future.
articles.body: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is reporting that Johny Srouji, senior vice president of hardware technologies, told Tim Cook he is “seriously considering” leaving Apple for another company in the near future. It was reported in October that Srouji was “evaluating his future at the tech giant.” While nothing is confirmed, it seems the executive is leaning toward not having a future at Cupertino. If Srouji leaves, he would be just the latest in a string of high-profile shakeups in the company’s C-suite. COO Jeff Williams announced his retirement in July, which led to some shifting of roles. But things have only accelerated in December, with AI chief John Giannandrea stepping down, policy lead Lisa Jackson and general counsel Kate Adams announcing plans to retire, and UI design lead Alan Dye departing for Meta, all in the last few days. Apple has struggled somewhat to find its footing as the industry further embraces AI. Now Tim Cook is tasked with trying to stem the bleeding, while being subject to rumors of his own departure. Gurman, who is usually reliable, has said those rumors are premature, but it still adds to the uncertainty surrounding what is typically one of the more stable companies in Silicon Valley.

articles.title: Apple hardware vp Johny Srouji reportedly tells staff “I don’t plan on leaving anytime soon.”
articles.summary:
After a string of exec departures from Apple, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported a few days ago that Srouji, who oversees the chips that have helped iPhones, Macs, and other devices lead their categories, had discussed leaving for another company.
Today, Gurman reports the exec sought to calm employees, sending a message to his division that said “I love my team, and I love my job at Apple, and I don’t plan on leaving anytime soon.”

articles.title: SC: PRF descobre carga clandestina de emagrecedor em bateria de carro | G1
articles.standfirst: Os envolvidos foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos. O compartimento da bateria do veículo foi adaptado com baterias de moto para esconder os produtos clandestinos.
articles.summary: Os envolvidos foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos. O compartimento da bateria do veículo foi adaptado com baterias de moto para esconder os produtos clandestinos.
articles.body:
Mais de 60 itens - entre ampolas de emagrecedores, frascos de anabolizantes e cigarros eletrônicos - foram flagrados sendo transportados clandestinamente na BR-101 em Joinville , cidade mais populosa de Santa Catarina , no Norte do estado.

Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF),o motorista e o passageiro contaram que alugaram o veículo para fazer uma viagem rápida de ida e volta até Foz do Iguaçu (PR), cidade que faz fronteira com o Paraguai. Os dois foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos.

Durante a revista pessoal, os agentes encontraram ampolas de emagrecedores escondidas nas roupas dos suspeitos e caixas de medicamentos sob as palmilhas dos calçados.

Ao serem questionados se havia mais irregularidades, um dos ocupantes confessou que existiam outros produtos escondidos sob o capô do carro.

No compartimento da bateria do veículo, adaptado com baterias menores de moto para abrir espaço, os policiais acharam os frascos de anabolizantes. Chaves específicas para retirar a peça estavam guardadas junto ao estepe.

Os dois foram encaminhados à delegacia da Polícia Federal de Joinville.

Segundo a PF, o transporte ou a comercialização de medicamentos clandestinos se enquadra no crime de adulteração de produto destinado a fins terapêuticos ou medicinais. A pena prevista é de 10 a 15 anos de reclusão.

articles.title: Not everyone is loving their new iPhone Duo
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo went on sale just over two weeks ago, but some early adopters have seen enough.
articles.body: For most new relationships, two weeks probably isn’t enough time to decide if you’re ready for long-term commitment. But two weeks with a new phone? You probably know. The iPhone Duo launched just over two weeks ago, and that’s been enough time for a subset of day-one buyers who aren’t loving the phone to make a decision: It’s time to end things. Also, they wanted their $2,000 back. This is to be expected, to an extent; the Duo just isn’t a phone for everyone. It’s an early adopter device — we called it “a messy, expensive good time” — and on top of that, the hinge appears to be suffering some first-gen growing pains. Despite all that, Apple seems to be selling Duos just fine, with new online orders projected to ship in January. As Apple’s customary 14-day return window came to a close, I reached out to a few people to learn more about why they brought their new Duos back. Some of it felt familiar — the outer screen is small, the cameras aren’t great — but other reasons were a little more surprising. Like the fact that the Duo’s whole proposition as a two-in-one device is sometimes a con, not a pro. [Media: “If I can have an iPad in my pocket, that would be great.” So thought Ben Seligson, a content creator, photographer, and now former iPhone Duo owner. After spending some time with the phone, he discovered that having a phone that’s also your iPad wasn’t always ideal. With two separate devices, Seligson told me, “Usually I’d throw a YouTube video on the iPad or throw a podcast up. And then I start cooking dinner and leave my iPad in one spot, but I’d have my phone in my pocket if I got a text, or I needed to set a timer or something like that.” With the Duo, the phone was also the iPad on the counter, so a quick reply became much more of an interruption. Less surprising: A couple of Duo owners I talked to weren’t interested enough in the form factor to try an Android foldable. Not for a lack of curiosity; rather, the iPhone lock-in feels too strong. Michael Hayes, another former Duo owner, says, “I used to flip back and forth between Android and iOS about 10 years ago, and I think I still have a Pixel in a drawer somewhere … Unless something massive changes, I’m locked into the ecosystem now.” Seligson has been tempted by Samsung’s foldables in the past. “A year ago when the Fold 7 came out I was kind of thinking about it,” he says. “But my whole family uses FaceTime; I’m on FaceTime with them all the time. I’ve got the Mac, I’ve got the iPad. So there’s just too many reasons not to try it.” Both Hayes and Seligson switched back to slab-style iPhones rather than other foldables. Fayethe Vongsouvanh, an art director, envisioned using the Duo for editing photos and planning their wedding. They had the misfortune of a cracked screen on the second day of owning the Duo. “At the time, I was at home recovering from hand surgery, so I knew there was no way I was too rough with it,” says Vongsouvanh. They were able to get a replacement quickly, but a number of other quirks led them to return that one, too. Weight was the biggest factor. “The phone is just too heavy and bulky for my daily use,” they say. [Media: Even though things didn’t work out, the Duo seems to have had an impact on the people I spoke to. “There’s a specialness that the Duo has that I kind of miss,” says Seligson. “It felt different, and it didn’t feel like the same phone everyone’s had for the last ten years.” Spending time with the Duo has inspired others to look at old form factors with a fresh perspective. Vongsouvanh enjoyed writing and drawing with the Duo’s inner screen and an Apple Pencil and has been inspired to pick up an older device more often. “I’ll definitely start using my old iPad Pro with a Paperlike screen protector more often,” they say. For Hayes, the Duo led him to downsize. “If there’s one thing the Duo did, it steered me toward the regular Pro instead of the Pro Max this time because it felt comically big after using the Duo.” Maybe small phones have a chance after all. If you’re still waiting for your Duo, there’s some good news; Apple’s holiday return policy kicked in on November 6th, so anyone who’s just getting their phone will have until January 8th, 2027, to return it for a full refund. Even if you don’t end up keeping the phone, you’re probably in for a good time. I’m still using it as my daily driver a few weeks later, and it keeps managing to surprise me with new tricks. But keep an eye on that return window — just in case.

articles.title: New Shaquille O’Neal game show draws ridicule over absurd premise
articles.summary: ‘Can You Hide... Shaq?’ is coming to ABC
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal is set to become the unlikely star of a new hide-and-seek-inspired game show, in which contestants will be tasked with concealing his 7-foot-1-inch frame.

The former NBA star will feature in ABC's Can You Hide... Shaq? , hosted by comedian Nicole Byer.

According to Variety , the show will see eight contestants competing to hide the 7ft 1in sports legend in plain sight around Dallas.

The series logline reads: "In the fast, funny and unpredictable challenges, contestants first split into two teams, each with a set mission and time clock.

"The team that completes its mission with the fewest spottings earns immunity for one team member in the next round, who then becomes team captain.

"The teams must work together toward one greater mission: earning prize money to add to the 'Shaq-pot' that will ultimately be claimed by one winner."

Shaq has promised plenty of fun for viewers.

He said in a statement: "I'm 7-foot-1. I'm not exactly easy to miss.

"I love meeting people wherever I go, but for years I've always wondered, could somebody actually make me disappear? Well, we finally decided to put it to the test.

"We turned it into a real competition, and I can't wait for you to see the creative, ridiculous ways they tried to hide me in plain sight.

"The stakes are high, and so is the prize. But you know me, we're gonna have some fun along the way."

On social media, the concept quickly drew ridicule, with one person comparing it to a sketch from 30 Rock .

They shared a photo of Alec Baldwin's network executive character, Jack Donaghy, speaking to Tina Fey's TV writer character, Liz Lemon, alongside the caption: "The premise is simple, Lemon: Contestants must hide Shaquille O'Neal from the people of Dallas. If this works, the network is ready to greenlight similar shows like 'Will You Co-Sign Lenny Dykstra's Loan?' and 'Can You Convince a Georgia Football Player to Call an Uber?'"

Shaq previously revealed how 12 months of success in 1996 forced him to maintain a level of focus that helped shape the rest of his career.

During that single year, Shaquille joined the Los Angeles Lakers after four seasons with the Orlando Magic, represented the United States at the Atlanta Olympics, was selected for the NBA's 50th Anniversary Team, released his third studio album, You Can't Stop the Reign, and starred as a genie in the fantasy comedy Kazaam.

Shaq told People magazine: "That was probably one of my years where I had to be focused every day."

He added: "I'm a guy that likes to go up and down with my focus on purpose, of course, because I always like to get away from it and then get back. But that year, there was so much coming, so much expectation, so many opportunities."

Can You Hide... Shaq? will premiere with two episodes on Thursday, December 3, at 9 p.m. on ABC and the ESPN app. Episodes will stream on Hulu the next day.

articles.title: Sharge’s eye-catching MacBook charger is over 25 percent off
articles.summary: The Sharge Pixel 140 Charger is down to $69.88 ($24 off) right now. You can also score discounts on DJI’s Mobile 8 smartphone gimbal and a Lego-esque Warthog set.
articles.body: Looking for a MacBook and device charger that’s as stylish as it is capable? Both Amazon and Sharge are selling the Pixel 140W GaN charger for $69.88 and $69.90, respectively, a $24 discount on its usual price. If you’re not in need of that much wattage but like the style, Sharge is also selling the 67W version for $19.90 ($30 off) or the 100W version for $59.90 ($16 off). [Product: Sharge Pixel 140 GaN Charger | The Pixel 140 delivers up to 140W of power when using only one of its three USB-C ports, which Sharge says is capable of taking a 16-inch MacBook Pro from a flat battery to 50 percent charge in just 25 minutes. It’s 47 percent smaller than the MacBook’s included charging brick as well, which is great if you’re tight on bag space or travel frequently. The pixel display on the side has configurable brightness and orientation, and displays your current charging wattage. Other deals to consider * Halo fans looking for a fun weeknight project can grab Mattel’s Brick Shop Warthog on Amazon for $62.99 ($12 off), which is the lowest price we’ve seen on the brick-ified UNSC replica. The 935-piece set lets you recreate a 1:22 scale model of the iconic land vehicle, and includes a 1:64 scale metal version as well. * Windows users with Mac Mini envy might consider the Lenovo Yoga Mini, which is currently discounted to $599.99 ($460 off) at Best Buy as part of the retailer’s early Black Friday promo. The compact desktop PC features an Intel Core Ultra 5 processor, 16GB of LPDDR5X memory, and 512GB of storage; it also has several fun features, including automated lighting around the system and Wi-Fi presence sensing. * While modern smartphone camera stabilization has improved dramatically, there are still plenty of situations where a motorized gimbal can help you capture a smoother shot. Fortunately, the DJI Osmo Mobile 8 is currently on sale at Amazon for $89 ($20 off), nearly matching its best price to date. It features 360-degree horizontal panning and over 10 hours of battery life on a single charge.

articles.title: A temporary stay of execution for the Cybertruck.
articles.summary:
Production of the controversial EV was supposed to wind down spring 2027, but Elon Musk is now extending the deadline through the end of summer. Musk admits this is “not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint,” adding “there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what’s the point?” Musk muses. Some Tesla fans have been unusually critical of the decision, while others have predictably fallen in line.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Video Review - IGN
articles.summary: Monster Hunter Outlanders reviewed by Hayes Madsen, played on iOS (iPhone 14 Plus), also available on Android."Monster Hunter Outlanders is simply one of those games that has too much stuff; it's overflowing with mobile-style fluff to keep track of, much of which gets in the way of enjoying that strong gameplay formula it clearly has. In many ways, it's genuinely remarkable how ambitious Outlanders is, and how deftly it manages to adapt the brilliance of Monster Hunter World into a smaller package. The smart streamlining of combat still keeps the intensity of hunts alive, while being more playable in short bursts. And while there's enough good here to keep you engaged, it equally comes with no shortage of frustrations in monetization, roadblocks, and the headache of endless menu management. That means, ultimately, Outlanders doesn't reach the heights of its console counterparts, but if you can go in with tempered expectations, the heart of Monster Hunter is still there."

The smart streamlining of combat still keeps the intensity of hunts alive, while being more playable in short bursts. And while there's enough good here to keep you engaged, it equally comes with no shortage of frustrations in monetization, roadblocks, and the headache of endless menu management. That means, ultimately, Outlanders doesn't reach the heights of its console counterparts, but if you can go in with tempered expectations, the heart of Monster Hunter is still there."

articles.title: Arjun Bijlani opens up about fatherhood, shares the values he wants to instil in son Ayaan; says, "I feel it’s my responsibility to lead by example"
articles.summary: Actor Arjun Bijlani has opened up about fatherhood and the values he hopes to instil in his son, Ayaan.
articles.body: Actor Arjun Bijlani has opened up about fatherhood and the values he hopes to instil in his son, Ayaan. In an exclusive quote shared with IANS, the ‘Naagin’ actor believes that parenting goes beyond teaching children the difference between right and wrong, as it also involves leading by example.Emphasizing the importance of kindness, respect and empathy, Arjun shared that he wants his son to grow up as a confident, independent and compassionate individual who respects everyone.Speaking about the values he wishes to pass on to his son, Arjun believes that parenting is as much about leading by example as it is about teaching. “I think kindness, respect and empathy are extremely important. As a father to Ayaan, I feel it’s my responsibility to lead by example. Children observe everything we do, so they learn more from our actions than our words. I want Ayaan to grow up being confident, independent, respectful towards everyone and, most importantly, a good human being.”Recalling the things he loved doing as a child, the actor admitted that he sometimes misses the carefree days when life was all about playing outdoors and spending time with friends. However, fatherhood has given him an opportunity to revisit those beautiful moments. “I loved playing outdoors with friends, spending hours doing absolutely nothing and not having to worry about time! I do miss those carefree days sometimes. But now, having Ayaan in my life gives me an opportunity to relive some of those childhood moments. Whether it’s playing with him, enjoying his little stories or seeing his excitement about school activities like Children’s Day, I get to experience that magic all over again,” he shared.Talking about his fondest childhood memories ahead of Children’s Day, Arjun shared, “Children’s Day was always exciting because it was one day when school felt more like a celebration than studies! I remember the fun, performances, games and spending time with friends. Now, as a father, I get to experience that excitement all over again through Ayaan. He looks forward to Children’s Day celebrations at school, and seeing his excitement makes me nostalgic about my own childhood. It’s lovely to see how some traditions never change!”Arjun Bijlani married Neha Swami on May 20, 2013. The couple are parents to a son, Ayaan Bijlani.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more.
